title: Equivalences of spaces detected on homotopy fibers
statement:
Use spaces, Kan complexes, homotopy fibers and weak homotopy equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $X,Y,S,T$ be Kan complexes, let $r:X\to S$, $q:Y\to T$, $u:X\to Y$ and $v:S\to T$ be maps, and specify a homotopy from $qu$ to $vr$. Suppose $v$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Then $u$ is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if, for every vertex $s\in S$, the induced map
$$\operatorname{hofib}_{s}(r)\longrightarrow\operatorname{hofib}_{v(s)}(q)$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. The fiber map sends a point $x$ together with a path from $r(x)$ to $s$ to $u(x)$ and the path obtained by composing the specified homotopy with the image under $v$ of that path, with all higher simplices retained. Neither vertical map is assumed to be a Kan fibration. Empty spaces and empty homotopy fibers are allowed.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 3.3.7.1 (00ZN), equivalently Proposition 3.2.8.1 for Kan bases, applied after path-space fibration replacement of both vertical maps: Example 3.1.8.10, Construction 3.4.0.3 and Remark 3.4.0.6; Propositions 3.4.0.7 and 3.4.0.9 compare strict fibers with homotopy fibers (Section 3.4, 0106). This is the homotopy-commutative, homotopy-fiber formulation. Read online, not archived in literature/. These identifiers are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags.

proof.text:
Write $H:qu\simeq vr$, $F_s=\operatorname{hofib}_s(r)$ and $G_s=\operatorname{hofib}_{v(s)}(q)$ using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Put $E=P(r)$ and $E'=P(q)$, with endpoint maps $R:E\to S$, $Q:E'\to T$ and projections $e:E\to X$, $e':E'\to Y$. By [lem-coef-space-path-fibration-replacement], $R,Q$ are Kan fibrations, the constant-path sections $\delta_X:X\to E$, $\delta_Y:Y\to E'$ are weak equivalences, and the strict vertex fibers of $R,Q$ are the homotopy fibers of $r,q$. Since $e\delta_X=1_X$ and $e'\delta_Y=1_Y$, the projections also induce bijections on components and isomorphisms on every positive-degree based group. The total spaces $E,E'$ are Kan: fill a horn in the base, then lift that simplex through the fibration. Their strict fibers are exactly $F_s,G_s$, hence are Kan by lifting horns over the constant base simplex.

We construct an actual strict square before using naturality. Over $E$, the paths $H_{e(-)}$ and $v(\gamma)$ define a map $E\times\Lambda_1^2\to T$, with edges $01$ and $12$ respectively. The inclusion $\Lambda_1^2\hookrightarrow\Delta^2$ is inner anodyne directly from the definition of inner fibration. Apply [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product] to this inner horn inclusion and the degreewise injection $\varnothing\hookrightarrow E$, and interchange the two product coordinates. Since the Kan complex $T$ fills inner horns, $T\to\Delta^0$ is an inner fibration; the resulting lifting property extends the map to $E\times\Delta^2\to T$. Its edge $02$, together with $ue$, defines $U:E\to E'$ satisfying $QU=vR$ and $e'U=ue$ strictly. On the fiber at $s$, this is the specified map $\phi_s$ with path $H_x\cdot v(\gamma)$. Any two such coherent composites are homotopic relative to the two given edges: apply the same inner pushout-product statement to $\Lambda_1^2\hookrightarrow\Delta^2$ and the degreewise injection $E\times\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow E\times\Delta^1$, and interchange product coordinates to extend the two fillers and their common horn to $E\times\Delta^1\times\Delta^2$. Restricting to edge $02$ gives the homotopy, preserving both endpoints and therefore all fiber maps.

By [lem-coef-kan-realization-serre], $|R|,|Q|$ are Serre fibrations. By the natural finite-limit assertion of [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], their fibers are $|F_s|,|G_s|$ and their strict square is the realization of $(U,v)$. Apply [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence] to these two Serre fibrations and this strict square. At every chosen fiber vertex this gives natural exact sequences, component actions, orbit identifications and stabilizers. The unpointed orbit identification also holds for an empty fiber: if a total-space component mapped to the chosen base component, choose a path from the image of a point in that component to the base vertex and lift it, using the path-lifting clause of the same Serre statement. Its endpoint would lie in the supposedly empty fiber. Thus the relevant total-space component fiber is empty too; the empty fiber-component set has the unique action and empty orbit set, and no pointed sequence is needed there. Identify their total-space groups and components with those of $X,Y$ by $e,e'$. The equality $e'U=ue$ makes the total-space comparison exactly $u_*$ and the base comparison is $v_*$. At $z=(x,\gamma)\in F_s$ and $z'=U(z)$ the based maps to $S,T$ become $r_{\gamma,*}$ and $q_{H_x\cdot v\gamma,*}$: evaluation of the universal path gives a homotopy from $re$ to $R$, and on a based cube its boundary follows precisely $\gamma$; the corresponding evaluation in $E'$ has boundary path $H_x\cdot v\gamma$. This is the defining change of base point on homotopy classes of cubes. Write $i,j$ for the fiber-to-total maps after these identifications. All exact sequences, actions and stabilizer statements used below refer to these identified sequences. No fibration hypothesis on $r$ or $q$ has been introduced.

source.place: Example 3.1.8.10 for mapping-path replacement; explicit parameterized horn filling supplies the strict square. Hovey Lemma 2.4.16, Corollary 3.6.2 and Lemma 3.2.4 give the realization and exact-sequence route already stated by the cited DAG nodes.

proof.text: Suppose first that $u$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, and fix $s$. Its map on components and that of $v$ are bijective. The orbit identifications in [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence] therefore make $\pi_0\phi_s$ bijective on orbit sets: these orbit sets are the fibers of $\pi_0r$ and $\pi_0q$ over $[s]$ and $[v(s)]$. Put $P=\pi_1(S,s)$ and $P'=\pi_1(T,v(s))$. The map $v_*:P\to P'$ is an isomorphism and $\pi_0\phi_s$ is equivariant. At every $z=(x,\gamma)$ its source stabilizer is $\operatorname{im}(r_{\gamma,*}:\pi_1(X,x)\to P)$, and the target stabilizer is $\operatorname{im}(q_{H_x\cdot v\gamma,*}:\pi_1(Y,u(x))\to P')$. Commutativity and the isomorphism $u_*$ show that $v_*$ carries the first subgroup onto the second. An equivariant map of transitive orbits with the same stabilizer is bijective: write the orbit elements as $g\cdot[z]$, and two such elements have the same image exactly when their quotient lies in that stabilizer. Thus the map on each orbit is bijective, and bijectivity on orbit sets proves $\pi_0\phi_s$ bijective. If one component set is empty, the bijection on orbit sets forces both to be empty; no base point was chosen for that case.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.8.1, proof in both directions; agent-expanded homotopy-fiber formulation using the natural exact sequence and component actions, with explicit diagram chases.

proof.text: Still suppose $u$ is a weak equivalence. Fix any $z=(x,\gamma)\in F_s$ and $n\geq1$. Use the exact sequences of [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence], with base-point transports as in step 1. To prove injectivity of $\phi_{s,*}$ on $\pi_n$, take $b$ mapping to $1$. Since $u_*$ is injective, $i_*b=1$, so $b=\partial c$ for some $c\in\pi_{n+1}(S,s)$. Then $\partial'v_*c=1$, whence $v_*c=q_*d'$ for some $d'\in\pi_{n+1}(Y,u(x))$. Lift $d'$ to $d$ by the isomorphism $u_*$; naturality and injectivity of $v_*$ give $c=r_*d$. Consequently $b=\partial r_*d=1$. For surjectivity take $b'\in\pi_n(G_s,z')$. Lift $j_*b'$ to $a\in\pi_n(X,x)$ by $u_*$. Its image under $r_*$ is $1$, since $v_*$ is injective and $q_*j_*b'=1$. Write $a=i_*b$. The element $b'(\phi_{s,*}b)^{-1}$ lies in $\ker j_*$, so it is $\partial'c'$ for some $c'\in\pi_{n+1}(T,v(s))$. Lift $c'$ to $c$ by $v_*$. Naturality now gives $b'=\phi_{s,*}((\partial c)b)$. This is a group calculation even when $n=1$ and never assumes commutativity. Together with step 2 and the definition of weak equivalence in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], it proves every $\phi_s$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.8.1, proof in both directions; agent-expanded homotopy-fiber formulation using the natural exact sequence and component actions, with explicit diagram chases.

proof.text: Conversely assume every $\phi_s$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. In particular its component map is bijective and equivariant for the isomorphism $v_*:\pi_1(S,s)\to\pi_1(T,v(s))$. It therefore induces a bijection on orbit sets (an equivariant bijection and an isomorphism of acting groups preserve and reflect membership in a common orbit). By [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence], this is exactly the map from the fiber of $\pi_0r$ over $[s]$ to the fiber of $\pi_0q$ over $[v(s)]$. Since $\pi_0v$ is bijective, these fiberwise bijections prove $\pi_0u$ bijective: for surjectivity choose the unique source base component of a given target component and use its fiberwise surjectivity; for injectivity two source components with the same image have the same base component and fiberwise injectivity applies. Every base component has a vertex representative, and empty component fibers cause no exception.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.8.1, proof in both directions; agent-expanded homotopy-fiber formulation using the natural exact sequence and component actions, with explicit diagram chases.

proof.text: For positive-degree groups choose $x\in X$, set $s=r(x)$, $z=(x,\mathrm{const}_s)$ and $z'=\phi_s(z)$. For $n\geq1$ use the natural exact sequences of [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence]. If $a\in\pi_n(X,x)$ satisfies $u_*a=1$, then $r_*a=1$ by injectivity of $v_*$. Thus $a=i_*b$ for $b\in\pi_n(F_s,z)$. Now $j_*\phi_{s,*}b=1$, so $\phi_{s,*}b=\partial'c'$ for some $c'\in\pi_{n+1}(T,v(s))$. Lift $c'$ to $c$ by $v_*$ and use injectivity of $\phi_{s,*}$ and naturality to get $b=\partial c$. Hence $a=1$. For surjectivity let $a'\in\pi_n(Y,u(x))$ and choose $c\in\pi_n(S,s)$ with $v_*c=q_*a'$. Naturality gives $\phi_{s,*}(\partial c)=\partial' q_*a'$, the distinguished point. If $n=1$, the relevant $\phi_{s,*}$ is the bijection on $\pi_0$ from the fiber equivalence; otherwise it is an isomorphism on $\pi_{n-1}$. In either case $\partial c$ is the distinguished point. Exactness gives $a\in\pi_n(X,x)$ with $r_*a=c$. Then $a'(u_*a)^{-1}$ lies in $\ker q_*$, so equals $j_*b'$ for some $b'\in\pi_n(G_s,z')$. Lift $b'$ to $b$ by $\phi_{s,*}$. We have $u_*((i_*b)a)=a'$. Thus $u_*$ is an isomorphism on every positive-degree based group, including the nonabelian fundamental group.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.8.1, proof in both directions; agent-expanded homotopy-fiber formulation using the natural exact sequence and component actions, with explicit diagram chases.

proof.text: Step 4 gives bijectivity on components and step 5 gives all positive-degree isomorphisms at vertices. Each point of a geometric realization lies in a simplex and is joined within that simplex to a vertex. Changing a base point along this path identifies the homotopy-group map with the vertex-based map; at degree one this identification is conjugation by the path. The same observation applies in step 3 to fiber realizations. Therefore these are precisely the weak homotopy equivalences defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. If $S$ is empty, $X$ is empty, and bijectivity of $\pi_0v$ forces $T$, then $Y$, to be empty, proving the vacuous fiber case directly. With nonempty bases, the orbit arguments already include empty fibers and empty total spaces. Both implications have now been proved for the specified homotopy and its induced fiber maps.
